summary: At Chuck Schumer's AI Insight Forum on November 29, 2023, Sony Music Entertainment's Dennis Kooker set out the company's stance on AI and copyright. He reported close to 10,000 deepfake takedowns, about 200 active conversations with AI startups and established players (some involving potential equity investments), and asked Congress to adopt five principles on generative AI. He also criticized the tech industry's "fair use" position on training AI models with music.
one_line: Sony Music's Dennis Kooker told a US Senate AI forum about nearly 10,000 deepfake takedowns, AI partnerships, and five principles for generative AI.
key_facts: On November 29, 2023, US Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer held an AI Insight Forum on the role of creative copyright and IP in AI development.
Dennis Kooker, Sony Music Entertainment's President of Global Digital Business & US Sales, spoke at the Forum on Sony's position on AI and copyright law.
Kooker said Sony Music Entertainment has sent "close to 10,000 takedowns" to platforms hosting unauthorized deepfakes that SME artists asked it to remove.
Kooker said platforms use loopholes in the law as an excuse to drag their feet or not take deepfakes down when requested.
Kooker said "Every stream of a deep fake takes streams and royalty payments away from the legitimate artist."
Kooker praised the No FAKES Act, which he said would create a federal property right in one's voice or visual likeness.
Sony Music has "roughly 200 active conversations taking place with startups and established players" about AI-related products and tools, some including potential equity investments.
SME recently announced a generative AI project with The Orb and David Gilmour, in partnership with Legacy Recordings and AI company Vermillio.

Kooker said recent Copyright Office filings show the tech industry and speculative financial investors want governments to believe in a "very distorted view of copyright" in which music is fair use for training.

Sony asked Congress to embrace five principles: consent, compensation and credit; confirm that copying music to train AI is not fair use; prevent voice and likeness cloning without express permission; incentivize accurate recordkeeping; and assure transparency for consumers and artists.

MBW noted a week earlier that no Sony Music artists were in the initial cohort of YouTube's 'Dream Track' AI voice-cloning project, which included Warner Music Group and Universal Music Group artists.

Anthropic and Stability AI argued in USCO submissions that training LLMs on copyrighted material is fair use, while Universal Music Group rejected that notion; Ed Newton-Rex resigned from Stability AI over its position.
